title: Text and Language
full_title: Text, Tokens and Classical Language Models
tagline: Text as data, tokenisation, n-gram language models, perplexity and word embeddings
summary: A language model assigns probabilities to text. This course starts from text as data, builds tokenisers, n-gram language models and their evaluation by perplexity, and learns word embeddings — the ideas on which neural language models are built.

chapters.title: Text as data
chapters.summary: Characters and Unicode, words and corpora, Zipf’s law and the statistics of language.

chapters.title: Tokenisation
chapters.summary: Word, character and subword tokenisers: byte-pair encoding, WordPiece, unigram language models and byte-level tokenisers.

chapters.title: N-gram language models
chapters.summary: The chain rule of probability, Markov assumptions, counting and smoothing.

chapters.title: Evaluating language models
chapters.summary: Likelihood, cross-entropy, perplexity and bits per byte.

chapters.title: Word embeddings
chapters.summary: Distributional semantics, word2vec, GloVe and the geometry of embedding spaces.

chapters.title: Text classification
chapters.summary: Bag-of-words models, embeddings and neural classifiers for sentiment, topic and intent.

chapters.title: Linguistic structure
chapters.summary: Morphology, syntax and semantics, and the tasks of classical NLP: tagging, parsing and named entities.
